trustTitle: You are trusting whoever runs the bot
trustLede: TGPORTAL is not an end-to-end tunnel past the operator. It is better to host one yourself.
trustP1: Messages you send a Telegram bot land on the computer running the program. It downloads files and sends them into Delta Chat there. Anyone who can read that machine can read what you bridged.
trustItems: Telegram user ids, names, and message bodies sent to the bot
Pairing codes and which Telegram is tied to which Delta Chat (in the database)
Sticker, GIF, image, and video files while they sit in cache
In persona mode: BotFather tokens you register, and the keys of ghost Delta Chat accounts
trustP2: Delta Chat still encrypts traffic on the wire to chatmail. That does not hide plaintext from tgportal itself. The runner is a participant.
trustP3: A public instance such as @tgdeltabridgebot is convenient for trying the product. Using it means you accept that operator’s machine. Do not bridge anything you would not hand to them.
trustP4: Then the only runner is you. See self-host. Operators who serve other people should publish a privacy policy (repo docs/privacy.md) and never log tokens.
personaLede: Register your own Telegram bot. Each remote user becomes a stable ghost Delta Chat account that talks to you as themselves.
personaWhyP1: Personal mode is you, the portal bot, and one Delta Chat. Fine for “my stickers, my chat.”
personaWhyP2: Persona mode is for people who already have (or want) a Telegram bot of their own. Friends and groups message your bot. On Delta Chat you should see them, not a labeled dump from a shared bridge account.
personaGhostsP1: For each person who messages your bot, it makes a real Delta Chat account (name and photo from Telegram). Next time it’s the same account.
personaGhostsP2: That ghost delivers the person’s message to you as a normal 1:1 — no prefix, no “via TGPORTAL.” When you reply, the program sends it out through your BotFather bot.
personaGhostsP3: Ghost tables are separate from personal-mode pairs. Alice pairing the public portal bot does not reuse Alice’s persona ghost.
personaSetupItems: Set mode: persona or both, and PERSONA_ACCOUNT_QR (a dcaccount: / dclogin: URI used to provision ghosts).
/pair on the portal bot and finish on Delta Chat. This saves your Delta Chat identity so ghosts can write to you without another invite.
Create a bot with BotFather. Copy the token. Never paste it into issues or chats.
In a private chat with the portal bot: /pair-bot <TOKEN> [https://t.me/YourBot]
personaLimits: Limits: persona.max_ghosts, persona.max_bots. List with /bots. Stop with /unpair-bot [id|@user]. Re-run /pair-bot after unpair to start the same bot again.
personaGroupsLead: Off by default. Enable persona.allow_groups: true, then:
personaGroupsItems: Add the persona bot to the Telegram group.
BotFather → your bot → Bot Settings → Group Privacy → Turn off. Otherwise Telegram only delivers mentions and commands.
Posts become a Delta Chat group named TG: …. Each speaker is their ghost; you are a member.
Your replies in that DC group go to Telegram as the bot, not as the original users.
personaTrustP1: The instance that stores the BotFather token is your Telegram bot. Ghost account keys live under ./data. If you give /pair-bot to someone else’s public TGPORTAL, you are handing them the bot and every conversation it will carry. Prefer self-hosting. See trust.
personaRepo: Repo operator notes: docs/persona.md, design: persona-design.md.
pairingLede: Nothing is forwarded until a Telegram user is linked to a Delta Chat chat.
pairingP1: This is mode: personal (also available under both). For owner-owned bots see persona.
pairingP2: Using a hosted bot means you trust that runner. Prefer your own instance.
pairingTgItems: Open the bot in a private 1:1 (e.g. @tgdeltabridgebot) and send /start or /pair. Groups are rejected so codes do not leak.
You get a QR of the Delta Chat invite plus an 8-character code (about 30 minutes).
Open the invite in Delta Chat / ArcaneChat and accept the chat.
pairingDcItems: Message the Delta Chat bot while unpaired (or send /pair).
Open that link on Telegram. Pairing is active immediately.
pairingCmdItems: /send_pack — reply to a sticker to bridge the whole pack (if bridge.sticker_packs is on)
pairingRepo: Full walkthrough in the repo: docs/pairing.md.
selfLede: Recommended. You keep the token, the database, and the ghost keys. Pick one path: build the binary, or download a release.
selfNeedLead: Both ways need the same runtime pieces after you have a tgportal binary:
selfNeedItems: deltachat-rpc-server on PATH (match the project’s rpc-client major; this repo uses v2.56.x APIs)
A chatmail / Delta Chat provider for make init / tgportal init
selfConfig: Then copy config.example.yml → config.yml and .env.example → .env. Data default is ./data. Never commit .env, config.yml, or data/.
selfWay1P: Use this when you have Go 1.22+ and want to compile from git. The Makefile is the supported entrypoint.
selfWay1Release: All-in-one static binary (stripped, version stamped) goes to dist/tgportal:
selfWay2: Way 2 — download the binary from a release
selfWay2P: Use this when you do not want a Go toolchain. GitHub Actions publish archives on each tag v*: tgportal_<tag>_<os>_<arch>.tar.gz (Windows .zip) plus checksums.txt.
selfWay2Items: Open the latest release or the releases list.
Download the archive for your OS/CPU (examples: linux_amd64, linux_arm64, darwin_arm64, windows_amd64).
Unpack, mark executable, put it next to config.yml and .env.
selfWay2Note: Replace VERSION with the tag without the leading v if the asset name uses that form (see the release notes). You still need deltachat-rpc-server on PATH; the release is only the Go bot.
selfPreview: Landing preview while developing: make run-landing → http://127.0.0.1:5173.
